technical_and_design_decisions: Refactor ledger tests to mock MSP dependencies rather than relying on full security context setup.
Define channel configuration transaction format using Protocol Buffers to ensure backward compatibility and clear serialization.
Implement peer upgrade handling with data migration validation hooks during peer startup.
Restrict chaincode invocation endpoints to reject system chaincodes other than LCCC unless explicitly privileged.
Structure Node.js SDK into modular packages (Client, Peer, Orderer, User) compatible with Fabric v1.0 gRPC protocols.
assumptions: A single software developer will execute all design, coding, documentation, and testing tasks.
Existing fabric-sdk-node repository structure is available and requires core feature implementation for Fabric v1.0 compatibility.
The underlying Go codebase for Fabric v1.0 block structure is largely defined, requiring final migration in remaining ledger modules.
Documentation will be published via Markdown / Sphinx documentation tools used by the Hyperledger project.

activities.activity_name: Documentation and Getting Started Guide Updates (U1, U6)
activities.activity_description: Update project documentation to include a clear getting started guide for v1.0, add notice/links directing users seeking a stable platform to v0.6, and organize navigation.
Define and document the structure, fields, and expected values for new-channel configuration transactions, integrating references from Gerrit change 1795.

activities.activity_name: Peer Upgrade & Protocol Change Migration Framework (U3)
activities.activity_description: Develop peer upgrade procedures and data persistence logic to allow protocol updates and patches (via System Chaincode) without loss of ledger data.

activities.activity_name: Ledger Code Refactoring & MSP Test Decoupling (U4)
activities.activity_description: Update remaining ledger code and unit tests to use the new block structure, and decouple ledger unit tests from MSP security dependencies.

activities.activity_name: v1.0 Architecture Visual Aids & Demo Scripts (U5)
activities.activity_description: Create architectural diagrams, visual aids, and automated demonstration scripts illustrating the v1.0 architecture and runtime behavior for stakeholders.
Implement validation logic to enforce that invocation requests only target LCCC or standard user chaincodes, blocking unauthorized system calls.
Develop Node.js SDK modules for interacting with Fabric v1.0 peers and orderers, including enrollment, transaction proposal creation, and event handling.
Perform end-to-end integration testing across ledger changes, chaincode invocation validation, peer upgrades, and Node.js SDK interactions.
